title: Enhancing LLM-based Hatred and Toxicity Detection with Meta-Toxic Knowledge Graph
measurement_description: The paper evaluated the performance of Large Language Models (LLMs) on binary classification for toxicity and hate speech detection. It specifically aimed to mitigate false positive misjudgments (caused by excessive sensitivity to sensitive topics like religion, race, and gender) and false negatives (caused by a lack of domain knowledge) by supplementing LLMs with a constructed meta-toxic knowledge graph.
findings: While religion is not the main focus, the study found that LLMs often misjudge contexts involving sensitive attributes like religion due to an extreme sensitivity to certain keywords. By incorporating a meta-toxic knowledge graph that explicitly maps out implicit toxic meanings and stereotypes (e.g., extracting hate triplets linking Muslims to terrorism, or documenting the downplaying of Christian/Muslim persecution), the MetaTox method successfully guided models to better understand underlying semantics, significantly reducing the false positive rate while improving overall detection accuracy.
